text:
Predicates:
Taller(x, y) ::: x is taller than y.
Blocks(x, y) ::: x can block y's shooting.
Jumps(x) ::: x jumps when shooting.
GreatShooter(x) ::: x is a great shooter.
Shoots(x, y) ::: x shoots at y.
Man(x) ::: x is a man.
Michael ::: Michael (constant).
Windy ::: Windy (constant).

Premises:
∀x ∀y (Taller(x, y) → Blocks(x, y)) ::: If a man is taller than another man, the taller one can block the other's shooting.
∀x (Taller(Michael, x)) ::: Michael is taller than everyone else in his class.
∀x ∀y ∀z ((Taller(x, y) ∧ Taller(y, z)) → Taller(x, z)) ::: If x is taller than y, and y taller than z, then x is taller than z.
Peter ::: Peter (constant).
Taller(Peter, Michael) ::: Peter is taller than Michael.
∀x (Jumps(x) → GreatShooter(x)) ::: Every shooter who can jump when shooting is a great shooter.
¬Blocks(Windy, Michael) ::: Michael cannot block Windy's shooting.

Conclusion:
GreatShooter(Windy) ::: Windy is a great shooter.
